## Policies

### Peer Review

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Type** | Single anonymized review. Submissions are first assessed by the editors; suitable papers are "typically" sent to at least two reviewers; the editors decide. Editors do not handle papers they wrote or that come from family members, colleagues or related interests (https://www.sciencedirect.com/journal/journal-of-economic-behavior-and-organization/publish/guide-for-authors, retrieved 2026-11-23) |
| **Transferable / Cascade?** | Elsevier's article transfer service exists: a manuscript transferred through it does not need a second submission fee (same guide). Which journals the service offers from this one was not read |
| **Reviewer reports published?** | Blank. No statement on the pages read |
| **Typical R+R rounds** | SciRev summary: 1.5 review rounds on average and 1.8 review reports on average (https://scirev.org/journal/journal-of-economic-behavior-and-organization/, retrieved 2026-11-23; based on the 15 reviews SciRev lists, see Reviewer Pool Characteristics; the 1.8 reports figure is reproduced by the 12 listed reviews that reached a review round, 22 reports in all) |
| **Reviewer recommendations** | Blank. No source. Authors may appeal an editorial decision once per submission under Elsevier's appeal policy (guide for authors) |

### AI Policy

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Has journal-specific AI policy?** | Partly. The guide for authors has a "Declaration of generative AI use" section that points to Elsevier's publisher-wide GenAI policy (https://www.sciencedirect.com/journal/journal-of-economic-behavior-and-organization/publish/guide-for-authors, retrieved 2026-11-23) |
| **Explicit permission gate?** | No gate found. Use is allowed under human oversight, with a statement required |
| **Leniency (1-5)** | 3 (allowed with a mandatory statement placed in the manuscript; this pass's own scale, 3 = disclosure statement required in the manuscript, 4 = brief note at submission, 5 = no disclosure) |
| **Summary** | AI tools may support authors but not replace human thinking; authors remain accountable for checking AI output, including references that may be fabricated. A statement naming the tool and reason is added at the end of the manuscript at first submission and appears in the published work. Basic grammar, spelling and reference checking is exempt. AI cannot be an author. Editors and reviewers may not upload unpublished manuscripts into generative AI tools. Retrieved 2026-11-23 |
| **Source URL** | https://www.sciencedirect.com/journal/journal-of-economic-behavior-and-organization/publish/guide-for-authors |

### Preprint Policy

> Journal wording from the guide for authors (retrieved 2026-11-23); general terms from Elsevier's sharing policy, https://www.elsevier.com/about/policies-and-standards/sharing (retrieved 2026-11-23).

| Stage | Allowed? | Notes |
|-------|----------|-------|
| Pre-submission | Yes | The guide says authors may share preprints under Elsevier's article-sharing policy and that sharing a preprint does not count as prior publication; the sharing policy says preprints can be shared anywhere at any time |
| Under review | Yes | The journal offers free posting on SSRN during submission, public once the paper passes the initial desk review; the choice has no effect on the editorial process (guide for authors) |
| Post-acceptance (AAM) | Yes, with embargo | Immediately on a personal homepage or blog, or by updating a preprint on arXiv or RePEc; on institutional repositories after an embargo. Embargo: 36 months for this ISSN in Elsevier's "Journal Specific Embargo Periods 2025" workbook (https://assets.ctfassets.net/o78em1y1w4i4/B9Hf8A898d6upwp0Uq2Wp/58aab9d0f341d2cf581bcb090d7c7705/Embargos-per-journal.xlsx, read 2026-11-23, row 0167-2681) |
| Version of Record | Subscription article: Elsevier's sharing terms; open-access article: free reuse under a Creative Commons licence | See Open Access |

## Format

> Source: the guide for authors, https://www.sciencedirect.com/journal/journal-of-economic-behavior-and-organization/publish/guide-for-authors, read 2026-11-23.

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Article types accepted** | Theoretical and empirical research on economic decision, organization and behavior, and on economic change; the aims text welcomes work on the interrelations of economics with biology, psychology, law, anthropology, sociology, finance, marketing, political science and mathematics (guide for authors, "Aims and scope"). The page does not list article types beyond research articles; Crossref lists all 2534 records in the window as journal-article type (https://api.crossref.org/works?filter=issn:0167-2681,from-pub-date:2021-01-01) |
| **Word limit** | Blank. No word or page limit for the main text appears in the guide |
| **Word limit negotiability** | Blank. No source |
| **Abstract limit** | At most 250 words, concise, factual, able to stand alone, avoiding references; 1 to 7 keywords in English; required "highlights" of 3 to 5 bullet points of at most 85 characters each, in a separate editable file |
| **Reference limit** | No cap. Any consistent style is accepted at submission; the journal's style is applied at proof stage; DOIs are asked for where available |
| **Supplementary material** | Encouraged; submitted with the manuscript, posted unedited; preferred file size 150 MB per file and 1 GB in total. Research data: "Option C" applies, meaning data must be deposited in a relevant repository, or a statement given explaining why not, which appears in the published article |
| **Figure/Table limits** | No count limit read. Tables must be editable text; figure resolution minimums are given (guide for authors) |
| **Style / submission format** | Word (.doc/.docx) or LaTeX (.tex) source, not PDF; Word in a single-column layout; title page with names, affiliations (where the work was carried out) and a corresponding author; acknowledgements in a separate section before the references; a funding statement; a competing-interests declaration; the submission fee must be paid at submission (guide for authors) |

### Framing Requirements

- **Mandatory framing?** Scope is the stated screen: a paper "may be rejected by the Editors without being sent for review" if inconsistent with the aims and scope or the style requirements, and the US$175 submission fee is non-refundable (https://www.sciencedirect.com/journal/journal-of-economic-behavior-and-organization/publish/guide-for-authors, retrieved 2026-11-23).
- **What kind of engagement?** Research on economic decision, organization and behavior, and on change, structure and institutional evolution; interdisciplinary links are "particularly welcome"; empirical work that "probes close to the core of the issues in theoretical dispute" is encouraged (aims text, same page).
- **Article type and length**: research articles; abstract at most 250 words, 1 to 7 keywords, highlights required; no main-text length limit read (same page).
- **Special-issue framing seen**: three open calls on the home page, each with a named guest-editor team: economic cycles (deadline 31 March 2027), bounded rationality (31 December 2026) and fertility and family dynamics (30 May 2027) (https://www.sciencedirect.com/journal/journal-of-economic-behavior-and-organization, retrieved 2026-11-23).
- **Consequences of ignoring it**: rejection without review is possible and the fee is not refunded (guide for authors). Whether that happens in practice is not stated beyond the SciRev immediate rejections (Review Cycle Time).

### Practical Concerns

| Concern | Detail |
|---------|--------|
| **IRB requirement strictness** | All studies with human participants require a statement of ethical approval, guidelines followed and informed consent, including the date and reference number of any approval; where approval is not required, the statement must say why and confirm protections used (https://www.sciencedirect.com/journal/journal-of-economic-behavior-and-organization/publish/guide-for-authors, retrieved 2026-11-23). Laboratory and field experiments are a stated focus, so this applies to a large share of papers (aims text; 98 titles carry laboratory or online-experiment wording and 58 randomized or field-experiment wording, overlap not removed, of 2534) |
| **Single-author acceptance** | Single-author records: 374 of 2463 Crossref records with author lists (15.2%), 2021-2026 (retrieved 2026-11-23). Authorship changes are not considered after acceptance (guide for authors) |
| **Independent scholar friendliness** | No independent-scholar rule on the pages read. Affiliations on the title page refer to where the work was carried out; only the corresponding author's affiliation is used for agreement eligibility (guide for authors, retrieved 2026-11-23) |
| **Data transparency requirement** | Data must be deposited in a relevant repository or a statement given explaining why not, which is published with the article ("Option C"); authors are encouraged to co-submit a data article to Data in Brief or MethodsX (guide for authors, retrieved 2026-11-23). No replication-package check is described on the pages read |
| **OPSEC compatibility** | Single anonymized review: reviewers see author identities (guide for authors, retrieved 2026-11-23). Preprints are allowed and do not count as prior publication, so authors cannot count on anonymity; SSRN posting is optional (same page) |
| **AI use** | Statement required in the manuscript at first submission when AI tools were used, apart from basic grammar and reference checks; AI cannot be an author (guide for authors, retrieved 2026-11-23) |
| **Open access and cost** | Submission fee US$175, non-refundable; subscription route has no publication fee; gold open access costs USD 3,640 excluding taxes (https://www.sciencedirect.com/journal/journal-of-economic-behavior-and-organization/publish/open-access-options, retrieved 2026-11-23) |
| **Originality screening** | The journal may check manuscripts with Elsevier screening tools (guide for authors, retrieved 2026-11-23) |

## Strategic Notes

> Each statement below follows from a fact recorded above and names it. Where the evidence does not support a statement, the field says so.

### Hard Blockers

- **Fee at submission**: a US$175 submission fee is charged for new and unsolicited manuscripts and is non-refundable, and the paper is considered only after payment (Open Access, Practical Concerns; guide for authors).
- **Scope and style screen**: a paper inconsistent with the aims and scope, or not meeting the style requirements, may be rejected without review (Framing Requirements).
- **Required files**: highlights (3 to 5 bullets of at most 85 characters), an abstract of at most 250 words and Word or LaTeX source files, not PDF (Format).
- **Human-subjects statement**: any study with human participants needs an ethics statement, with date and reference number of approval or a reason for exemption (Practical Concerns).
- **Data**: a repository deposit or a published statement explaining why data cannot be shared (Practical Concerns).
- **AI**: a statement is required when AI tools were used beyond basic checks, and AI cannot be an author (AI Policy).

### Soft Tax

- **Time**: publisher figures of 87 days to a decision after review and 292 days to acceptance (Review Cycle Time; averages undefined); SciRev self-reports of 9.6 to 65.1 weeks for first-round outcomes on the 12 of 15 listed reviews that reached a review round (Review Cycle Time).
- **Cost of open access**: USD 3,640 for gold open access; the subscription route is free of publication fees (Open Access).
- **Green deposit delay**: 36 months embargo for repository posting of the accepted manuscript, though a personal homepage or arXiv or RePEc update is allowed immediately (Preprint Policy).
- **Non-anonymity**: single anonymized review means reviewers see author identities (Practical Concerns).

### Best Suited For

- Behavioural, experimental and institutional economics: OpenAlex topic assignments of 2983 (experimental behavioural economics) and 1839 (decision-making) and 98 laboratory-style titles of 2534 (Subject Density, Methodological Preferences).
- Work that links economics to another discipline: the aims text names nine disciplines it welcomes (Framing Requirements).
- Papers with a laboratory experiment that bears on a theoretical dispute: stated in the aims text (Methodological Preferences).
- Team papers: 2089 of 2463 Crossref records with author lists have two or more authors (84.8%) (Voice & Style).

### Not Recommended For

- Qualitative, interview-based or philosophical work: 0 title hits for interview, ethnography or qualitative wording and 2 for philosophy wording out of 2534 (Methodological Preferences). Titles are a floor, so this shows rarity, not rejection.
- Authors needing a stated acceptance rate or word limit before choosing: neither is printed on the pages read (Metrics, Format).
- Authors who need anonymised review: the model is single anonymized (Peer Review).

### Rejection Fallback Chain

> No source states where rejected authors usually go. The guide says a manuscript sent through Elsevier's article transfer service does not require a second submission fee (Peer Review), and the rows below name a corpus neighbour and the publisher family; neither is a claim about acceptance odds.

| Rank | Journal | Why this fallback works |
|------|---------|------------------------|
| 1 | Another Elsevier journal offered by the article transfer service | The transfer carries the submission without a second fee (guide for authors); which titles it offers from this journal was not read |
| 2 | [American Economic Review](american-economic-review.md) | Entry exists in this corpus; general-interest economics with a stated screen on breadth. A different level of selectivity, so only for papers with a general-interest case (see that entry) |
| 3 | [Journal of Economic Methodology](journal-of-economic-methodology.md) | Entry exists in this corpus; shares the economics subject area. No fit evidence collected here |
